newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon construction recovers slightly - Banque Audi.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon construction recovers slightly - Banque Audi.

text.p: Lebanon's construction sector recovered slightly in the third quarter but is still operating at well below last year's level, Banque Audi said in its latest quarterly economic report.
Estimates of unsold housing stock ranged from 60,000 to 80,000 units, the bank said.
Construction permits issued by the Association of Engineers of Beirut in the third quarter totalled 5.2 million square metres, 154 percent up on the second quarter.
However, the total of permits issued in the first nine months -- for 11.8 million square metres -- was 48.7 percent down on the same period of 1995, the bank said.
Third quarter cement deliveries rose 21.5 percent to 1,163,000 tonnes, bringing the total for the first nine months of 1996 to 2,810,000 -- 5.4 percent down on the same period of 1995.

"The slowdown in the construction sector actually depicts that of private investment which, according to our estimates, registered over the first nine-month period a real regression of 12.5 percent relative to last year's equivalent period," the report said.
This was a slight improvement on the first semester when the regression of private investment was 15.5 percent on the first six months of 1995.
Banque Audi is one of Lebanon's leading commercial banks and the reports prepared by its economic analysis unit are well regarded in financial and business circles.

It said the causes of the slowdown included the precariousness of Lebanon's real estate market, the absence of any organised form of housing loans and high interest rates on the Lebanese pound which were reducing investment and increasing financial savings.

However, despite the present slump annual housing needs were expected to be 40,000 units a year for the next 10 years and average auto-financing margins of 70 percent were helping to sustain prices while preventing an expansion of the real estate bubble and the appearance of an acute crisis.
"Finally, the launching in 1996 by many big banks of housing loan programmes is an undeniable support to demand," Banque Audi said.
